title: Acropolis of Toniná, Chiapas
summary: The acropolis of Toniná, a Maya city in Chiapas, was built on a mountain top that was reshaped into seven platforms. INAH gives them a height of 245 feet and facades 1,050 feet wide. The city reached its peak in the Classic period, between 600 and 900 CE.

uncertainty.note: INAH dates the site's peak to 600-900 AD; it does not date when the acropolis was built, and Yucatán Magazine says the city was likely founded in the 2nd century CE with clearer history from the 6th. Start 600 is the beginning of that peak. End is the present.

reviewer_note: Shape stepped_pyramid with 7 tiers. The 245 ft height and 1,050 ft width are INAH figures converted to metres (74.7 m and 320 m); the INAH page does not say whether 245 ft is measured from the plaza. The acropolis has no sourced construction date: the 600 start is the site's Classic peak, so the phases are a stand-in. Coordinates are the OSM point for the whole archaeological site, not the acropolis.
